verdict.rationale: Rive's docs describe an automatic Revision History that tracks all changes, including multi-user edits. You can preview a revision and restore it non-destructively with Edit Current Revision, which copies it to a new entry at the top of the list. That covers browsing and restoring earlier states, but the evidence never mentions naming milestones or comparing versions, and previewing one revision is not the same as a comparison. Missing for 10: naming/labeling milestone versions, side-by-side or diff comparison of revisions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, full version history lets me name milestones, compare, and restore any earlier state of a file

citations.quote: Rive saves your files automatically as you work. Even if multiple people are working on the same file at the same time, Rive tracks all changes and stores them in the Revision History.
Select a revision to preview it and press the Edit Current Revision button. This copies the selected revision and creates a new entry at the top of the list.
This guarantees that even restoring revisions is non-destructive, and you can always go back to the previous version of the file.
